title: Torsion kernel and cokernel do not change the rank of a module
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma controls how far rank is from being an isomorphism invariant over a domain: a map M to M' whose kernel and cokernel are torsion modules has equal ranks at source and target (statement lines 5026-5030). The author's proof is a hint rather than a full argument (proof lines 5033-5035): one has to tensor the map with the fraction field K and observe that both the kernel and the cokernel die, because every torsion module has zero tensor product with K. The two steps that a reader must supply are that this vanishing holds for an arbitrary torsion module, not just for a module of the shape R/I, and that the resulting exactness of the tensor sequence identifies the induced map of K-vector spaces as an isomorphism. With that, the equality of ranks is just the definition of rank as a dimension.
